A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 13-page SpatialMQA paper, including Appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that the manuscript content matches, with only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differing visually.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations on SpatialMQA in Tables 4–7, alongside dataset statistics and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original SpatialMQA evaluations, dataset statistics and error analyses, including the model and human results in Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and annotation procedures in Section 3 and the inference and tuning procedures in Section 5.1 are identical. No method component, model architecture or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5,392-sample, COCO2017-derived SpatialMQA benchmark, covering six spatial relations and the same out-of-image, first-person and third-person question types.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same seven open-source MLLMs, Gemini-1.5-flash, GPT-4o, random selection and human comparisons. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in Tables 5–7.

E3.justification: The training/development/test counts remain 3,780/536/1,076. Evaluation sample sizes, precision/recall/F1/accuracy metrics, tuning settings, ICL protocols and analysis controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 retain identical question-type and spatial-axis breakdowns, ICL-alignment experiments, image/option-count ablations and analysis of 200 error samples. The illustrative error cases also match.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the statement that results average three runs. Repeated-run disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout both PDFs.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 4 retains 48.14% accuracy for LoRA-tuned SpaceLLaVA, 40.20% for zero-shot GPT-4o and 98.40% for humans.

T1.justification: Section 2's task formulation and Table 2's coordinate-system and spatial-relation definitions are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about perspective substitution, image dependence and the substantial model–human performance gap.

C2.justification: Interpretations of image reliance, ICL alignment and error patterns are unchanged. Both versions state the same limitations concerning training-set scale and coverage of only six basic spatial relations.

D1.justification: The prompts, instruction formats, hyperparameters, hardware and annotation-tool details in Section 5 and Appendices A–F match. The code/data repository link is unchanged; v2's additional arXiv self-link supplies no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Table 1's benchmark comparison, Section 6's related-work discussion and the bibliography are identical. No cited work or substantive research positioning changes.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 25 May 2025 to v2 dated 8 August 2025. Manuscript wording, headings, author information and section structure, including the appendices, remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–12 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Pages 2–13 render identically, and the first-page visual difference is confined to the updated arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, results, figures, tables and appendices are unchanged. Updating the arXiv stamp and adding a self-link does not meaningfully alter the paper's evidence, clarity or reproducibility.
